prompt: The NONSEQ address is accepted in cycle 2. Toggle HREADY LOW in following data-phase cycles 3-6. Why does cycle-2 HREADY not satisfy the property, and how does asserting HRESETn LOW inside the window change the result?
expectedTakeaway: The configured contract fails only when the accepted cycle-2 address sees no completion in following cycles 3-6. Cycle-2 HREADY completed the preceding data owner while accepting this address, so it cannot satisfy the new transfer. HRESETn LOW cancels the obligation through disable iff. A timeout failure is a configured service-contract result, not by itself a universal AHB protocol-safety violation.
